protocolDescription: Fixed route of about 1-2 km in 5-15 sections, walked at a slow, steady pace once a week (UKBMS weeks: week 1 = 1-7 April, ... week 26 = 23-29 September), ideally 10:45-15:45. Count all butterflies seen within a fixed recording box: 2.5 m either side of the line and 5 m ahead (or 5 m on one side only, e.g. sea cliffs, woodland rides). Do not stop at hotspots, avoid double counting, do not count butterflies behind. One nominated recorder counts only what they see. Only complete walks are submitted. Minimum weather: 13-17 °C with at least 60% sunshine, or 17 °C or above; wind no more than Beaufort 5. Similar species may be netted and counts apportioned by the sample's proportions. Small and Essex skipper may be recorded as an aggregate. Sightings outside the recording box go in the notes.

Per section: % of the time the section was in sunshine, to the nearest 10% (sun casting a shadow counts). Per walk: shade temperature (°C), average sunshine (%), average wind speed (Beaufort 0-6) and wind direction.

Per section: length (m), grid reference near the mid-point, up to four habitat codes (G4 classification, 1-40, primary first) and up to four management codes (M1-M13, primary first), for habitats and management within 10 m either side of the line.
